# Requirements — `2025-11-25`

Every normative clause of the `2025-11-25` specification that the validator's registry carries — 153 in all, 59 judged from a recorded trace and 94 excluded with the reason below. A report names a clause by the ID used as each heading here; each entry quotes the specification verbatim and links to the published text. `mcp-trace-validator requirements --revision 2025-11-25 --format json` prints the same data as JSON.

## BASE

### BASE-001

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Requests MUST include a string or integer ID.

[`basic#requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#requests)

Judged by `base.request-id-type`.

### BASE-002

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Unlike base JSON-RPC, the ID MUST NOT be `null`.

[`basic#requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#requests)

Judged by `base.request-id-not-null`.

### BASE-003

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> The request ID MUST NOT have been previously used by the requestor within the same session.

[`basic#requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#requests)

Judged by `base.request-id-unique`.

### BASE-004

**MUST** · binds the client and server

[`basic#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#result-responses)

Judged by `base.result-id-matches`.

### BASE-005

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

[`basic#notifications`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#notifications)

Judged by `base.notification-no-id`.

### BASE-006

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Error responses MUST include an `error` field with a `code` and `message`.

[`basic#error-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#error-responses)

Judged by `base.error-shape`.

### BASE-007

**MUST** · binds the client and server

[`basic#error-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#error-responses)

Judged by `base.error-code-integer`.

### BASE-008

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> All messages between MCP clients and servers MUST follow the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification.

[`basic#messages`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#messages)

Judged by `base.jsonrpc-version`.

### BASE-009

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Error responses MUST include the same ID as the request they correspond to (except in error cases where the ID could not be read due a malformed request).

[`basic#error-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#error-responses)

Judged by `base.error-id-matches`.

### BASE-010

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Result responses MUST include a `result` field.

[`basic#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#result-responses)

Judged by `base.result-field`.

### BASE-011

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> The receiver MUST NOT send a response.

[`basic#notifications`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#notifications)

**Excluded.** A response to a notification carries no correlating ID, so it is indistinguishable on the wire from any other unsolicited response; unsolicited responses are flagged by base.result-id-matches and base.error-id-matches under BASE-004/BASE-009.

### BASE-012

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> All implementations MUST support the base protocol and lifecycle management components.

[`basic`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic)

**Excluded.** The umbrella clause the BASE and LIFE areas mechanize requirement-by-requirement; it has no observable beyond its constituents.

### BASE-013

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Clients and servers MUST support JSON Schema 2020-12 for schemas without an explicit `$schema` field

[`basic#implementation-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#implementation-requirements)

**Excluded.** Dialect support is validation behavior inside each implementation; a trace shows schemas exchanged, not how the receiver processed them.

### BASE-014

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Clients and servers MUST validate schemas according to their declared or default dialect.

[`basic#implementation-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#implementation-requirements)

**Excluded.** Whether validation happened, and against which dialect, is implementation-internal; validation outcomes need ground truth about inputs that a trace does not carry.

### BASE-015

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> They MUST handle unsupported dialects gracefully by returning an appropriate error indicating the dialect is not supported.

[`basic#implementation-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#implementation-requirements)

**Excluded.** Judging graceful handling requires knowing the receiver's supported-dialect set, which is not in the trace.

### BASE-016

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Clients and servers SHOULD document which schema dialects they support

[`basic#implementation-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#implementation-requirements)

**Excluded.** Documentation lives outside the protocol session entirely.

### BASE-017

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Schemas MUST be valid according to their declared or default dialect

[`basic#schema-validation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#schema-validation)

Judged by `base.schemas-valid-for-dialect`.

### BASE-018

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Certain key names are reserved by MCP for protocol-level metadata, as specified below; implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about values at these keys.

[`basic#_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#_meta)

**Excluded.** What an implementation assumes is internal; only conduct that follows from an assumption could surface, and attributing it requires the assumption.

### BASE-019

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> If specified, MUST be a series of labels separated by dots (`.`), followed by a slash (`/`); Labels MUST start with a letter and end with a letter or digit; interior characters can be letters, digits, or hyphens (`-`)

[`basic#_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#_meta)

Judged by `base.meta-key-format`.

### BASE-020

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Unless empty, MUST begin and end with an alphanumeric character (`[a-z0-9A-Z]`); MAY contain hyphens (`-`), underscores (`_`), dots (`.`), and alphanumerics in between

[`basic#_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#_meta)

Judged by `base.meta-key-format`.

### BASE-021

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Implementations SHOULD use reverse DNS notation (e.g., `com.example/` rather than `example.com/`).

[`basic#_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#_meta)

**Excluded.** Whether a syntactically valid prefix is reverse-DNS for its author cannot be decided without knowing the author's domain.

### BASE-022

**MUST** · binds the client

> Clients that support rendering icons MUST support at least the following MIME types:

[`basic#icons`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#icons)

**Excluded.** Icon rendering support is client-internal capability with no wire footprint; the conditional premise (that the client renders icons) is equally invisible.

### BASE-023

**MUST** · binds the client

> Consumers of icon metadata MUST take appropriate security precautions when handling icons to prevent compromise:

[`basic#icons`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#icons)

**Excluded.** The umbrella for consumer-side icon hygiene (fetch policy, size limits, origin checks) — all consumer-internal conduct after the recorded session ends.

### BASE-024

**MUST** · binds the client

> Clients MUST reject icon URIs that use unsafe schemes and redirects, such as `javascript:`, `file:`, `ftp:`, `ws:`, or local app URI schemes.

[`basic#icons`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#icons)

**Excluded.** Rejection is client-side handling after receipt; the trace records the icon metadata served, not what the client did with it.

### BASE-082

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Supported dialects: Implementations MUST support at least 2020-12 and SHOULD document which additional dialects they support

[`basic#schema-dialect`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#schema-dialect)

**Excluded.** Restates BASE-013's dialect floor and BASE-016's documentation SHOULD as the section's third numbered rule, unconditionally where BASE-013 scopes itself to schemas without an explicit `$schema` (the same restatement shape as TRAN-049 to TRAN-024). Excluded for BASE-013's reason: dialect support is validation behavior inside each implementation, and a trace shows the schemas exchanged, not how the receiver processed them.

### BASE-085

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client and server

> Implementations using an HTTP-based transport SHOULD conform to this specification, whereas implementations using STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.

[`basic#auth`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#auth)

**Excluded.** Credential retrieval from the environment is process-local conduct with no wire footprint, and the HTTP half defers to the authorization specification, which `sources.json` records as out of scope and TRAN-009 records as the boundary. One entry for the sentence's SHOULD and SHOULD NOT, as BASE-068 enters it at 2026-07-28.

### BASE-086

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Implementors are RECOMMENDED to use JSON Schema 2020-12.

[`basic#schema-dialect`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#schema-dialect)

Judged by `base.schemas-use-2020-12`.

### BASE-087

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> `image/png` - PNG images (safe, universal compatibility) `image/jpeg` (and `image/jpg`) - JPEG images (safe, universal compatibility) Clients that support rendering icons SHOULD also support:

[`basic#icons`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#icons)

**Excluded.** Extends BASE-022's client-internal rendering-support premise: neither the support nor its absence reaches the wire, and the premise itself (that the client renders icons) is equally invisible.

## LIFE

### LIFE-001

**MUST** · binds the client

> The initialization phase MUST be the first interaction between client and server.

[`basic/lifecycle#initialization`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#initialization)

Judged by `lifecycle.first-interaction-initialize`.

### LIFE-002

**MUST** · binds the client

> The client MUST initiate this phase by sending an `initialize` request containing: Protocol version supported; Client capabilities; Client implementation information

[`basic/lifecycle#initialization`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#initialization)

Judged by `lifecycle.initialize-params`.

### LIFE-003

**MUST** · binds the client

> After successful initialization, the client MUST send an `initialized` notification to indicate it is ready to begin normal operations

[`basic/lifecycle#initialization`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#initialization)

Judged by `lifecycle.initialized-notification`.

### LIFE-004

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client

> The client SHOULD NOT send requests other than pings before the server has responded to the `initialize` request.

[`basic/lifecycle#initialization`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#initialization)

Judged by `lifecycle.client-requests-before-init-response`.

### LIFE-005

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the server

> The server SHOULD NOT send requests other than pings and logging before receiving the `initialized` notification.

[`basic/lifecycle#initialization`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#initialization)

Judged by `lifecycle.server-requests-before-initialized`.

### LIFE-006

**MUST** · binds the server

> If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version. Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports.

[`basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation)

Judged by `lifecycle.initialize-result-version`.

### LIFE-007

**MUST** · binds the client

> In the `initialize` request, the client MUST send a protocol version it supports.

[`basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation)

Judged by `lifecycle.initialize-protocol-version`.

### LIFE-008

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Both parties MUST: Respect the negotiated protocol version

[`basic/lifecycle#operation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#operation)

**Excluded.** After negotiation, neither stdio nor HTTP message payloads carry a per-message protocol version, so respect is not observable in message traffic. The one wire artifact — the HTTP `MCP-Protocol-Version` header — is judged under TRAN-017 and TRAN-018.

### LIFE-009

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Both parties MUST: Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated

[`basic/lifecycle#operation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#operation)

Judged by `lifecycle.negotiated-capabilities-only`.

### LIFE-010

**MUST** · binds the server

> The server MUST respond with its own capabilities and information:

[`basic/lifecycle#initialization`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#initialization)

Judged by `lifecycle.initialize-result-shape`.

### LIFE-011

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> This SHOULD be the latest version supported by the client.

[`basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation)

**Excluded.** The client's supported-version set is internal state with no wire footprint; the trace shows the version sent, not the versions available.

### LIFE-012

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> This SHOULD be the latest version supported by the server.

[`basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation)

**Excluded.** The server's supported-version set is internal state with no wire footprint; the trace shows the version answered, not the versions available.

### LIFE-013

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> If the client does not support the version in the server's response, it SHOULD disconnect.

[`basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation)

**Excluded.** Whether the client supports the answered version is client-internal; a continued session is only evidence of support if the premise is known. TRAN-018 warns on the adjacent observable (a mismatched MCP-Protocol-Version header).

### LIFE-014

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> For the stdio transport, the client SHOULD initiate shutdown by: First, closing the input stream to the child process (the server); Waiting for the server to exit, or sending `SIGTERM` if the server does not exit within a reasonable time; Sending `SIGKILL` if the server does not exit within a reasonable time after `SIGTERM`

[`basic/lifecycle#shutdown`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#shutdown)

**Excluded.** Stdin closure, signals, and process exit are host-OS actions outside the trace event vocabulary (transport-open/close/abort record that a transport ended, not who ended it or how).

### LIFE-015

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Implementations SHOULD establish timeouts for all sent requests, to prevent hung connections and resource exhaustion.

[`basic/lifecycle#timeouts`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#timeouts)

**Excluded.** Checks may not consult time: trace timestamps are informational by design (determinism rule, 02-architecture.md), so timing conduct cannot be judged.

### LIFE-016

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> When the request has not received a success or error response within the timeout period, the sender SHOULD issue a cancellation notification for that request and stop waiting for a response.

[`basic/lifecycle#timeouts`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#timeouts)

**Excluded.** Checks may not consult time: trace timestamps are informational by design (determinism rule, 02-architecture.md), so timing conduct cannot be judged.

### LIFE-017

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> However, implementations SHOULD always enforce a maximum timeout, regardless of progress notifications, to limit the impact of a misbehaving client or server.

[`basic/lifecycle#timeouts`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#timeouts)

**Excluded.** Checks may not consult time: trace timestamps are informational by design (determinism rule, 02-architecture.md), so timing conduct cannot be judged.

### LIFE-018

**MUST** · binds the client

> If using HTTP, the client MUST include the `MCP-Protocol-Version: <protocol-version>` HTTP header on all subsequent requests to the MCP server.

[`basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#version-negotiation)

Judged by `transport.protocol-version-header`.

### LIFE-019

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> SDKs and other middleware SHOULD allow these timeouts to be configured on a per-request basis.

[`basic/lifecycle#timeouts`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#timeouts)

**Excluded.** Binds an SDK's programming interface — what its callers can configure — which has no protocol representation at all.

### LIFE-020

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Implementations SHOULD be prepared to handle these error cases: Protocol version mismatch; Failure to negotiate required capabilities; Request timeouts

[`basic/lifecycle#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Preparedness is a property of the implementation, not of any session it took part in: a trace that happens to contain a version mismatch shows one case handled, and a trace without one evidences nothing. Where the handling has a wire form it is judged under the clause that states it, such as the version negotiation rules.

## TRAN

### TRAN-001

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Messages are delimited by newlines, and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines.

[`basic/transports#stdio`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#stdio)

**Excluded.** Framing is enforced at capture time: the JSON Lines trace format cannot represent an embedded-newline violation, so a parseable trace is evidence the rule held. Violations surface as capture-time parse failures, not as trace findings.

### TRAN-002

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST validate the `Origin` header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks

[`basic/transports#security-warning`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#security-warning)

**Excluded.** Judging Origin validation requires the server's configured allowlist, which recorded traces do not carry. Enforced instead as default-on policy in mcp-everything-server and exercised by its transport integration tests (roadmap M2).

### TRAN-003

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded.

[`basic/transports`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports)

**Excluded.** A violation cannot be judged from a trace: trace documents are UTF-8 by construction, so recorded messages prove nothing was mis-encoded among what was recorded — and absence is not evidence, because capture tooling may drop undecodable bytes (mcp-everything-server's tap skips non-UTF-8 SSE chunks and unparseable POST bodies). No offline check is sound.

### TRAN-004

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> The server MUST NOT write anything to its `stdout` that is not a valid MCP message.

[`basic/transports#stdio`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#stdio)

Judged by `transport.stdio-server-output-valid`.

### TRAN-005

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> The client MUST NOT write anything to the server's `stdin` that is not a valid MCP message.

[`basic/transports#stdio`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#stdio)

Judged by `transport.stdio-client-input-valid`.

### TRAN-006

**MUST** · binds the server

> The server MUST provide a single HTTP endpoint path (hereafter referred to as the MCP endpoint) that supports both POST and GET methods.

[`basic/transports#streamable-http`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#streamable-http)

**Excluded.** Recorded HTTP events carry status and conformance-relevant headers, not request lines, so endpoint topology is invisible in a trace. Enforced by mcp-everything-server's transport integration tests (roadmap M2).

### TRAN-007

**MUST** · binds the server

> If the `Origin` header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden.

[`basic/transports#security-warning`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#security-warning)

**Excluded.** Judging whether an Origin value is invalid requires the server's configured allowlist, which recorded traces do not carry (the TRAN-002 rationale). Enforced as default-on policy in mcp-everything-server with 403 tests (roadmap M2).

### TRAN-008

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> When running locally, servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1) rather than all network interfaces (0.0.0.0)

[`basic/transports#security-warning`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#security-warning)

**Excluded.** Socket binding is deployment state with no trace footprint. mcp-everything-server defaults to a loopback bind (the --bind clap default in src/main.rs), asserted by default_bind_is_loopback in tests/cli.rs.

### TRAN-009

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD implement proper authentication for all connections

[`basic/transports#security-warning`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#security-warning)

**Excluded.** Whether authentication is properly implemented is not decidable from one session's headers; authorization flows are their own scenario area (corpus/auth, post-M1) mirroring the official suite's `auth` suite.

### TRAN-010

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> The session ID SHOULD be globally unique and cryptographically secure (e.g., a securely generated UUID, a JWT, or a cryptographic hash).

[`basic/transports#session-management`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#session-management)

**Excluded.** Global uniqueness and entropy of an identifier cannot be established from the single sample a trace contains. mcp-everything-server's ids are pinned to the v4-UUID shape (OS RNG) and distinctness by session_ids_are_version_4_uuids_and_distinct in tests/http_policy.rs.

### TRAN-011

**MUST** · binds the server

> The session ID MUST only contain visible ASCII characters (ranging from 0x21 to 0x7E).

[`basic/transports#session-management`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#session-management)

Judged by `transport.session-id-visible-ascii`.

### TRAN-012

**MUST** · binds the client

> The client MUST handle the session ID in a secure manner, see Session Hijacking mitigations for more details.

[`basic/transports#session-management`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#session-management)

**Excluded.** Secure handling (storage, exposure, logging discipline) is client-internal behavior with no wire footprint beyond the echo requirement judged under TRAN-013.

### TRAN-013

**MUST** · binds the client

> If an `MCP-Session-Id` is returned by the server during initialization, clients using the Streamable HTTP transport MUST include it in the `MCP-Session-Id` header on all of their subsequent HTTP requests.

[`basic/transports#session-management`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#session-management)

Judged by `transport.session-id-echoed`.

### TRAN-014

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers that require a session ID SHOULD respond to requests without an `MCP-Session-Id` header (other than initialization) with HTTP 400 Bad Request.

[`basic/transports#session-management`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#session-management)

**Excluded.** Whether a server requires a session ID is server configuration a trace does not carry; without it, a non-400 answer to a session-less request is not evidence either way.

### TRAN-015

**MUST** · binds the server

> The server MAY terminate the session at any time, after which it MUST respond to requests containing that session ID with HTTP 404 Not Found.

[`basic/transports#session-management`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#session-management)

**Excluded.** Session termination is server-internal state; a trace cannot distinguish a terminated session (404 required) from a live one (404 forbidden).

### TRAN-016

**MUST** · binds the client

> When a client receives HTTP 404 in response to a request containing an `MCP-Session-Id`, it MUST start a new session by sending a new `InitializeRequest` without a session ID attached.

[`basic/transports#session-management`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#session-management)

**Excluded.** A 404 is attributed to the request it answered when the recording's order is unambiguous, but not to the moment the client read it: a recorder logs the status as it passes, and the client may already have sent further requests on the old session. Requests after the 404 therefore do not show the client ignored it, and a client that stops instead of reconnecting sends nothing to judge.

### TRAN-017

**MUST** · binds the client

> If using HTTP, the client MUST include the `MCP-Protocol-Version: <protocol-version>` HTTP header on all subsequent requests to the MCP server, allowing the MCP server to respond based on the MCP protocol version.

[`basic/transports#protocol-version-header`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#protocol-version-header)

Judged by `transport.protocol-version-header`.

### TRAN-018

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> The protocol version sent by the client SHOULD be the one negotiated during initialization.

[`basic/transports#protocol-version-header`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#protocol-version-header)

Judged by `transport.protocol-version-negotiated`.

### TRAN-019

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> For backwards compatibility, if the server does not receive an `MCP-Protocol-Version` header, and has no other way to identify the version - for example, by relying on the protocol version negotiated during initialization - the server SHOULD assume protocol version `2025-03-26`.

[`basic/transports#protocol-version-header`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#protocol-version-header)

**Excluded.** Which version a server assumed is internal state; subsequent traffic does not reveal it.

### TRAN-020

**MUST** · binds the server

> If the server receives a request with an invalid or unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version`, it MUST respond with `400 Bad Request`.

[`basic/transports#protocol-version-header`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#protocol-version-header)

Judged by `transport.unsupported-version-header-rejected`.

### TRAN-021

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client

> The client MAY capture, forward, or ignore the server's `stderr` output and SHOULD NOT assume `stderr` output indicates error conditions.

[`basic/transports#stdio`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#stdio)

**Excluded.** How a client interprets stderr is internal, and stderr bytes are not part of the protocol trace (the trace records MCP messages and transport lifecycle, not diagnostics channels).

### TRAN-022

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Clients SHOULD support stdio whenever possible.

[`basic/transports`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports)

**Excluded.** A client's supported-transport surface is a property of the implementation, not of any one session; a streamable-HTTP trace says nothing about whether stdio was available.

### TRAN-023

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Implementers who choose to support custom transports MUST ensure they preserve the JSON-RPC message format and lifecycle requirements defined by MCP.

[`basic/transports#custom-transports`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#custom-transports)

**Excluded.** The trace vocabulary covers stdio and streamable HTTP; custom transports are outside the capture universe by construction (TransportKind is closed per revision).

### TRAN-024

**MUST** · binds the client

> Every JSON-RPC message sent from the client MUST be a new HTTP POST request to the MCP endpoint.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** Adds to TRAN-049's verb obligation that each message ride a *new* POST to the MCP endpoint. A POST body is one JSON value, which a recorder writes as one payload, so more than one message in a POST is a batch array — TRAN-026 judges that. What remains — that the request was new rather than reused, and was addressed to the MCP endpoint — leaves no trace: the endpoint is not recorded.

### TRAN-025

**MUST** · binds the client

> The client MUST include an `Accept` header, listing both `application/json` and `text/event-stream` as supported content types.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

Judged by `transport.client-post-accept-header`.

### TRAN-026

**MUST** · binds the client

> The body of the POST request MUST be a single JSON-RPC request, notification, or response.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

Judged by `transport.http-post-single-message`.

### TRAN-027

**MUST** · binds the server

> If the server accepts the input, the server MUST return HTTP status code 202 Accepted with no body.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

Judged by `transport.accepted-input-status`.

### TRAN-028

**MUST** · binds the server

> If the server cannot accept the input, it MUST return an HTTP error status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request).

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** Whether input was acceptable is server-internal judgment, and the trace schema records HTTP request and response observations as independent events without request/response correlation, so which response answered which POST is not decidable offline; the official suite exercises this live and the conformance gate runs it.

### TRAN-029

**MUST** · binds the server

> If the input is a JSON-RPC request, the server MUST either return `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, to initiate an SSE stream, or `Content-Type: application/json`, to return one JSON object.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

Judged by `transport.success-content-type`.

### TRAN-030

**MUST** · binds the client

> The client MUST support both these cases.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** What a client could have handled is client-internal capability; a trace shows the case that occurred, not the cases supported.

### TRAN-031

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> The server SHOULD immediately send an SSE event consisting of an event ID and an empty `data` field in order to prime the client to reconnect (using that event ID as `Last-Event-ID`).

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** SSE framing is consumed at capture: the tap reassembles `data:` lines into messages and drops event IDs and `retry` fields, so SSE-frame-level conduct is invisible in a trace.

### TRAN-032

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> If the server does close the connection prior to terminating the SSE stream, it SHOULD send an SSE event with a standard `retry` field before closing the connection.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** SSE framing is consumed at capture: the tap reassembles `data:` lines into messages and drops event IDs and `retry` fields, so SSE-frame-level conduct is invisible in a trace.

### TRAN-033

**MUST** · binds the client

> The client MUST respect the `retry` field, waiting the given number of milliseconds before attempting to reconnect.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** Checks may not consult time: trace timestamps are informational by design (determinism rule, 02-architecture.md), so timing conduct cannot be judged.

### TRAN-034

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> The SSE stream SHOULD eventually include a JSON-RPC response for the JSON-RPC request sent in the POST body.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** Which HTTP stream delivered a message is not part of the trace vocabulary — events form a single capture-ordered sequence — so per-stream conduct cannot be judged from a recorded trace.

### TRAN-035

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> These messages SHOULD relate to the originating client request.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** Relatedness is a semantic judgment over message content, and which HTTP stream delivered a message is not part of the trace vocabulary — events form a single capture-ordered sequence — so per-stream conduct cannot be judged from a recorded trace.

### TRAN-036

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> After the JSON-RPC response has been sent, the server SHOULD terminate the SSE stream.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** Which HTTP stream delivered a message is not part of the trace vocabulary — events form a single capture-ordered sequence — so per-stream conduct cannot be judged from a recorded trace.

### TRAN-037

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the server

> Disconnection SHOULD NOT be interpreted as the client cancelling its request.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** How the server interpreted a disconnect is internal state; only conduct that follows from a misinterpretation could surface, and attributing it requires the interpretation.

### TRAN-038

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> To cancel, the client SHOULD explicitly send an MCP `CancelledNotification`.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** A wish to cancel is client intent with no observable of its own; a session without a cancellation is not evidence one was wanted.

### TRAN-039

**MUST** · binds the client

> The client MUST include an `Accept` header, listing `text/event-stream` as a supported content type.

[`basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server)

Judged by `transport.client-get-accept-header`.

### TRAN-040

**MUST** · binds the server

> The server MUST either return `Content-Type: text/event-stream` in response to this HTTP GET, or else return HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed, indicating that the server does not offer an SSE stream at this endpoint.

[`basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server)

Judged by `transport.get-content-type`.

### TRAN-041

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> These messages SHOULD be unrelated to any concurrently-running JSON-RPC request from the client.

[`basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server)

**Excluded.** Unrelatedness is a semantic judgment over message content, and which HTTP stream delivered a message is not part of the trace vocabulary — events form a single capture-ordered sequence — so per-stream conduct cannot be judged from a recorded trace.

### TRAN-042

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> The server MUST NOT send a JSON-RPC response on the stream unless resuming a stream associated with a previous client request.

[`basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server)

**Excluded.** Which HTTP stream delivered a message is not part of the trace vocabulary — events form a single capture-ordered sequence — so per-stream conduct cannot be judged from a recorded trace.

### TRAN-043

**MUST** · binds the server

> The server MUST send each of its JSON-RPC messages on only one of the connected streams; that is, it MUST NOT broadcast the same message across multiple streams.

[`basic/transports#multiple-connections`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#multiple-connections)

**Excluded.** Which HTTP stream delivered a message is not part of the trace vocabulary — events form a single capture-ordered sequence — so per-stream conduct cannot be judged from a recorded trace. A duplicated message in the capture order is also indistinguishable from a legitimately repeated notification.

### TRAN-044

**MUST** · binds the server

> If present, the ID MUST be globally unique across all streams within that session—or all streams with that specific client, if session management is not in use.

[`basic/transports#resumability-and-redelivery`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#resumability-and-redelivery)

**Excluded.** SSE framing is consumed at capture: the tap reassembles `data:` lines into messages and drops event IDs and `retry` fields, so SSE-frame-level conduct is invisible in a trace.

### TRAN-045

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Event IDs SHOULD encode sufficient information to identify the originating stream, enabling the server to correlate a `Last-Event-ID` to the correct stream.

[`basic/transports#resumability-and-redelivery`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#resumability-and-redelivery)

**Excluded.** SSE framing is consumed at capture: the tap reassembles `data:` lines into messages and drops event IDs and `retry` fields, so SSE-frame-level conduct is invisible in a trace.

### TRAN-046

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> If the client wishes to resume after a disconnection (whether due to network failure or server-initiated closure), it SHOULD issue an HTTP GET to the MCP endpoint, and include the `Last-Event-ID` header to indicate the last event ID it received.

[`basic/transports#resumability-and-redelivery`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#resumability-and-redelivery)

**Excluded.** Conditional on client intent (the wish to resume): a session that never disconnects owes nothing, and a recording cannot show a client wishing. When a resumption does occur its method and `last-event-id` header are both recorded, but absence proves nothing.

### TRAN-047

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> The server MUST NOT replay messages that would have been delivered on a different stream.

[`basic/transports#resumability-and-redelivery`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#resumability-and-redelivery)

**Excluded.** Which HTTP stream delivered a message is not part of the trace vocabulary — events form a single capture-ordered sequence — so per-stream conduct cannot be judged from a recorded trace.

### TRAN-048

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Clients that no longer need a particular session (e.g., because the user is leaving the client application) SHOULD send an HTTP DELETE to the MCP endpoint with the `MCP-Session-Id` header, to explicitly terminate the session.

[`basic/transports#session-management`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#session-management)

**Excluded.** Conditional on client intent (no longer needing the session). A teardown DELETE is recorded when it happens — `corpus/good/http-session.jsonl` carries one — but a session that ends without one may simply not have finished with it, so absence is not a violation.

### TRAN-049

**MUST** · binds the client

> The client MUST use HTTP POST to send JSON-RPC messages to the MCP endpoint.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

Judged by `transport.client-messages-use-post`.

### TRAN-138

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> The client SHOULD then "poll" the SSE stream by attempting to reconnect.

[`basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#sending-messages-to-the-server)

**Excluded.** The obligation arises when the server closes the connection without terminating the SSE stream, and that is connection- and SSE-frame-level conduct the capture consumes (TRAN-032's reason), so no trace shows when it arose. A later reconnecting `GET` is equally consistent with any other reason to open one, as for TRAN-046.

### TRAN-139

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> If the server closes the connection without terminating the stream, it SHOULD follow the same polling behavior as described for POST requests: sending a `retry` field and allowing the client to reconnect.

[`basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#listening-for-messages-from-the-server)

**Excluded.** SSE framing is consumed at capture: the tap reassembles `data:` lines into messages and drops event IDs and `retry` fields, so SSE-frame-level conduct is invisible in a trace. TRAN-032 is the same rule for streams a POST opened.

### TRAN-140

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Custom transports SHOULD document their specific connection establishment and message exchange patterns to aid interoperability.

[`basic/transports#custom-transports`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports#custom-transports)

**Excluded.** Binds a transport's documentation, not its messages: the artefact the clause asks for is a document, and no session can be evidence about whether one exists. Custom transports are outside the capture universe besides (TRAN-023).

## TOOL

### TOOL-001

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers that support tools MUST declare the `tools` capability:

[`server/tools#capabilities`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#capabilities)

Judged by `tools.capability-declared`.

### TOOL-002

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.tools.listChanged` is negotiated

> When the list of available tools changes, servers that declared the `listChanged` capability SHOULD send a notification:

[`server/tools#list-changed-notification`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#list-changed-notification)

**Excluded.** The trigger condition — the tool list actually changing — is server-internal state a recorded trace cannot evidence, so absence of the notification is never proof of violation.

### TOOL-003

**MUST** · binds the server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> `inputSchema`: JSON Schema defining expected parameters; MUST be a valid JSON Schema object (not `null`)

[`server/tools#tool`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#tool)

Judged by `tools.input-schema-object`.

### TOOL-004

**MUST** · binds the client

> For trust & safety and security, clients MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.

[`server/tools#tool`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#tool)

**Excluded.** How a client weighs annotations is internal trust policy with no wire footprint.

### TOOL-005

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> Tool names SHOULD be between 1 and 128 characters in length (inclusive).

[`server/tools#tool-names`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#tool-names)

Judged by `tools.name-length`.

### TOOL-006

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> The following SHOULD be the only allowed characters: uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), underscore (_), hyphen (-), and dot (.)

[`server/tools#tool-names`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#tool-names)

Judged by `tools.name-charset`.

### TOOL-007

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> Tool names SHOULD NOT contain spaces, commas, or other special characters.

[`server/tools#tool-names`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#tool-names)

Judged by `tools.name-charset`.

### TOOL-008

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> Tool names SHOULD be unique within a server.

[`server/tools#tool-names`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#tool-names)

Judged by `tools.name-unique`.

### TOOL-009

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> Servers that use embedded resources SHOULD implement the `resources` capability:

[`server/tools#embedded-resources`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#embedded-resources)

Judged by `tools.embedded-resource-capability`.

### TOOL-010

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> For backwards compatibility, a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block.

[`server/tools#structured-content`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#structured-content)

Judged by `tools.structured-content-text`.

### TOOL-011

**MUST** · binds the server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> If an output schema is provided: Servers MUST provide structured results that conform to this schema.

[`server/tools#output-schema`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#output-schema)

Judged by `tools.output-schema-structured-result`.

### TOOL-012

**MUST** · binds the server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> Servers MUST: Validate all tool inputs; Implement proper access controls; Rate limit tool invocations; Sanitize tool outputs

[`server/tools#security-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#security-considerations)

**Excluded.** Input validation, access control, rate limiting, and output sanitization are server-internal enforcement without a deterministic wire signature. Of the four duties, mcp-everything-server implements and tests input validation (tests/roundtrip.rs: tool_call_with_missing_required_argument_is_a_protocol_error and neighbors); access control beyond the transport-layer Host/Origin gate, rate limiting, and output sanitization are not in its scope — it serves fixed synthetic fixtures to a loopback-only harness.

### TOOL-013

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> Tool names SHOULD be considered case-sensitive.

[`server/tools#tool-names`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#tool-names)

**Excluded.** Name-comparison semantics are consumer-internal; tools.name-unique (TOOL-008) applies case-sensitive comparison in accordance with this clause.

### TOOL-014

**SHOULD** · binds the client · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> Clients SHOULD validate structured results against this schema.

[`server/tools#output-schema`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#output-schema)

**Excluded.** Client-side validation has no wire footprint; the server-side half of the contract is TOOL-011's check.

### TOOL-015

**SHOULD** · binds the client · only once `server.tools` is negotiated

> For trust & safety and security, there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations.

[`server/tools#user-interaction-model`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#user-interaction-model)

**Excluded.** A host application's approval UX is outside the protocol session; a trace shows invocations that happened, not the approvals that gated them.

### TOOL-047

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Applications SHOULD: Provide UI that makes clear which tools are being exposed to the AI model; Insert clear visual indicators when tools are invoked; Present confirmation prompts to the user for operations, to ensure a human is in the loop

[`server/tools#user-interaction-model`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#user-interaction-model)

**Excluded.** Binds the application's user interface — what it shows, when it asks, whether a person is there. None of it is a message, and MCP deliberately does not mandate an interaction model.

### TOOL-048

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Clients SHOULD provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction.

[`server/tools#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Binds what the client hands to a language model, which is downstream of the session entirely.

### TOOL-049

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Clients SHOULD: Prompt for user confirmation on sensitive operations; Show tool inputs to the user before calling the server, to avoid malicious or accidental data exfiltration; Validate tool results before passing to LLM; Implement timeouts for tool calls; Log tool usage for audit purposes

[`server/tools#security-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#security-considerations)

**Excluded.** Five client-side practices — confirmation prompts, showing inputs, validating results, timeouts, audit logs. Each happens inside the client or in its UI; none is a message.

## RES

### RES-001

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers that support resources MUST declare the `resources` capability:

[`server/resources#capabilities`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#capabilities)

Judged by `resources.capability-declared`.

### RES-002

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.resources.listChanged` is negotiated

> When the list of available resources changes, servers that declared the `listChanged` capability SHOULD send a notification:

[`server/resources#list-changed-notification`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#list-changed-notification)

**Excluded.** The trigger condition — the resource list actually changing — is server-internal state a recorded trace cannot evidence.

### RES-003

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.resources` is negotiated

> Servers SHOULD use this scheme only when the client is able to fetch and load the resource directly from the web on its own—that is, it doesn’t need to read the resource via the MCP server.

[`server/resources#https//`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#https//)

**Excluded.** Whether the client can fetch a URI on its own is a property of the client's environment, not of the recorded session.

### RES-004

**MUST** · binds the server · only once `server.resources` is negotiated

> Custom URI schemes MUST be in accordance with RFC3986, taking the above guidance in to account.

[`server/resources#custom-uri-schemes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#custom-uri-schemes)

Judged by `resources.uri-scheme-rfc3986`.

### RES-005

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST validate all resource URIs

[`server/resources#security-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#security-considerations)

**Excluded.** URI validation is server-internal enforcement; a trace shows the URIs exchanged, not whether the server vetted them. mcp-everything-server's read path is fail-closed — unknown or malformed URIs resolve to None — asserted by template_rejects_malformed_instantiations (src/resources.rs) and the unknown-URI protocol-error assertion in resources_surface_matches_the_scenarios (tests/roundtrip.rs).

### RES-006

**MUST** · binds the server · only once `server.resources` is negotiated

> Binary data MUST be properly encoded

[`server/resources#security-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#security-considerations)

Judged by `resources.blob-base64`.

### RES-007

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.resources` is negotiated

> For other use cases, servers SHOULD prefer to use another URI scheme, or define a custom one, even if the server will itself be downloading resource contents over the internet.

[`server/resources#https//`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#https//)

**Excluded.** The premise — whether the client could fetch the URI directly — is a property of the client's environment, not of the session (the RES-003 argument).

### RES-008

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.resources` is negotiated

> Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Resource not found: `-32002`; Internal errors: `-32603`

[`server/resources#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Whether a failure case actually occurred (the resource was absent, an internal fault happened) is server-side ground truth a trace does not carry.

### RES-009

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Access controls SHOULD be implemented for sensitive resources

[`server/resources#security-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#security-considerations)

**Excluded.** Which resources are sensitive and what controls guard them is deployment policy with no per-session observable.

### RES-010

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Resource permissions SHOULD be checked before operations

[`server/resources#security-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#security-considerations)

**Excluded.** Permission checks are server-internal enforcement; a trace shows the operations served, not the checks that admitted them.

## PROM

### PROM-001

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers that support prompts MUST declare the `prompts` capability during initialization:

[`server/prompts#capabilities`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#capabilities)

Judged by `prompts.capability-declared`.

### PROM-002

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.prompts.listChanged` is negotiated

> When the list of available prompts changes, servers that declared the `listChanged` capability SHOULD send a notification:

[`server/prompts#list-changed-notification`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#list-changed-notification)

**Excluded.** The trigger condition — the prompt list actually changing — is server-internal state a recorded trace cannot evidence.

### PROM-003

**MUST** · binds the server · only once `server.prompts` is negotiated

> The image data MUST be base64-encoded and include a valid MIME type.

[`server/prompts#image-content`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#image-content)

Judged by `prompts.image-content-encoding`.

### PROM-004

**MUST** · binds the server · only once `server.prompts` is negotiated

> The audio data MUST be base64-encoded and include a valid MIME type.

[`server/prompts#audio-content`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#audio-content)

Judged by `prompts.audio-content-encoding`.

### PROM-005

**MUST** · binds the server · only once `server.prompts` is negotiated

> Resources can contain either text or binary (blob) data and MUST include: A valid resource URI; The appropriate MIME type; Either text content or base64-encoded blob data

[`server/prompts#embedded-resources`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#embedded-resources)

Judged by `prompts.embedded-resource-shape`.

### PROM-006

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Implementations MUST carefully validate all prompt inputs and outputs to prevent injection attacks or unauthorized access to resources.

[`server/prompts#security`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#security)

**Excluded.** Validation thoroughness is implementation-internal; a trace shows the prompt traffic, not the vetting applied to it.

### PROM-007

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.prompts` is negotiated

> Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Invalid prompt name: `-32602` (Invalid params); Missing required arguments: `-32602` (Invalid params); Internal errors: `-32603` (Internal error)

[`server/prompts#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Whether a failure case actually occurred (the name was invalid, an argument was missing) is server-side ground truth a trace does not carry.

### PROM-008

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.prompts` is negotiated

> Servers SHOULD validate prompt arguments before processing

[`server/prompts#implementation-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#implementation-considerations)

Judged by `prompts.arguments-validated`.

### PROM-009

**SHOULD** · binds the client · only once `server.prompts` is negotiated

> Clients SHOULD handle pagination for large prompt lists

[`server/prompts#implementation-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#implementation-considerations)

**Excluded.** Client-side pagination handling is internal; a session whose lists fit one page exercises nothing.

### PROM-010

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Both parties SHOULD respect capability negotiation

[`server/prompts#implementation-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/prompts#implementation-considerations)

**Excluded.** Mechanized at the protocol level by LIFE-009's negotiated-capabilities-only check; this restatement adds no separately observable conduct.

## LOG

### LOG-001

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers that emit log message notifications MUST declare the `logging` capability:

[`server/utilities/logging#capabilities`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/logging#capabilities)

Judged by `logging.capability-declared`.

### LOG-002

**MUST NOT** · binds the server · only once `server.logging` is negotiated

> Log messages MUST NOT contain: Credentials or secrets; Personal identifying information; Internal system details that could aid attacks

[`server/utilities/logging#security`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/logging#security)

**Excluded.** Deciding whether free-form log data contains secrets or PII is semantic content analysis, not structural validation; offline heuristics would produce unsound, unfalsifiable verdicts — a fixed pattern list is deterministic but proves nothing about what it misses.

### LOG-003

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.logging` is negotiated

> Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Invalid log level: `-32602` (Invalid params); Configuration errors: `-32603` (Internal error)

[`server/utilities/logging#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/logging#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Whether a failure case actually occurred (the level was invalid for this server, configuration failed) is server-side ground truth a trace does not carry.

### LOG-004

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.logging` is negotiated

> Servers SHOULD: Rate limit log messages; Include relevant context in data field; Use consistent logger names; Remove sensitive information

[`server/utilities/logging#implementation-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/logging#implementation-considerations)

**Excluded.** Rate policy, context relevance, naming consistency, and redaction are semantic internals (the LOG-002 argument).

### LOG-005

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server · only once `server.logging` is negotiated

> Implementations SHOULD: Rate limit messages; Validate all data fields; Control log access; Monitor for sensitive content

[`server/utilities/logging#security`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/logging#security)

**Excluded.** Rate limiting, validation, access control, and monitoring are implementation-internal enforcement without trace-level observables.

## COMP

### COMP-001

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers that support completions MUST declare the `completions` capability:

[`server/utilities/completion#capabilities`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/completion#capabilities)

Judged by `completion.capability-declared`.

### COMP-002

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Implementations MUST: Validate all completion inputs; Implement appropriate rate limiting; Control access to sensitive suggestions; Prevent completion-based information disclosure

[`server/utilities/completion#security`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/completion#security)

**Excluded.** Input validation, rate limiting, and access control are implementation-internal enforcement without a deterministic wire signature.

### COMP-003

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.completions` is negotiated

> Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Method not found: `-32601` (Capability not supported); Invalid prompt name: `-32602` (Invalid params); Missing required arguments: `-32602` (Invalid params); Internal errors: `-32603` (Internal error)

[`server/utilities/completion#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/completion#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Whether a failure case actually occurred is server-side ground truth a trace does not carry.

### COMP-004

**SHOULD** · binds the server · only once `server.completions` is negotiated

> Servers SHOULD: Return suggestions sorted by relevance; Implement fuzzy matching where appropriate; Rate limit completion requests; Validate all inputs

[`server/utilities/completion#implementation-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/completion#implementation-considerations)

**Excluded.** Relevance ordering, fuzziness, rate policy, and input vetting are semantic internals without trace-level observables.

### COMP-005

**SHOULD** · binds the client · only once `server.completions` is negotiated

> Clients SHOULD: Debounce rapid completion requests; Cache completion results where appropriate; Handle missing or partial results gracefully

[`server/utilities/completion#implementation-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/completion#implementation-considerations)

**Excluded.** Debouncing and caching are client-internal and timing-shaped; checks may not consult time (determinism rule).

## PAGE

### PAGE-001

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> Page size is determined by the server, and clients MUST NOT assume a fixed page size

[`server/utilities/pagination#pagination-model`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/pagination#pagination-model)

**Excluded.** What a client assumes is internal state; the assumption has no wire footprint (MCP pagination requests carry no size parameter to inspect).

### PAGE-002

**MUST** · binds the client

> Clients MUST treat cursors as opaque tokens: Don't make assumptions about cursor format; Don't attempt to parse or modify cursors; Don't persist cursors across sessions

[`server/utilities/pagination#implementation-guidelines`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/pagination#implementation-guidelines)

Judged by `pagination.cursor-opacity`.

### PAGE-003

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Invalid cursors SHOULD result in an error with code -32602 (Invalid params).

[`server/utilities/pagination#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/pagination#error-handling)

Judged by `pagination.invalid-cursor-rejected`.

### PAGE-004

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD: Provide stable cursors; Handle invalid cursors gracefully

[`server/utilities/pagination#implementation-guidelines`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/pagination#implementation-guidelines)

**Excluded.** Cursor stability is cross-request server behavior over hidden state; gracefulness on invalid cursors requires knowing a cursor was invalid (the PAGE-003 argument).

### PAGE-005

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Clients SHOULD: Treat a missing `nextCursor` as the end of results; Support both paginated and non-paginated flows

[`server/utilities/pagination#implementation-guidelines`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/utilities/pagination#implementation-guidelines)

**Excluded.** How a client interprets a missing cursor, and what flows it supports, is client-internal; the wire-visible cursor discipline is PAGE-002's check.
